scores.doc: CDS 2025-2026, C9 (1,092 SAT submitters, 412 ACT submitters)

testPolicy.text: All first-year and transfer applicants must include scores from the ACT or SAT. AP or IB scores may be added but are not required and no longer replace the SAT/ACT. The ACT Science and Writing sections are optional; superscoring is accepted.

gpa.doc: CDS 2025-2026, C11-C12 left blank by Yale

cost.totalIncludes: Sum of the published 2026-27 line items: tuition 72,500 + student activity fee 185 + housing 12,080 + food 9,520 + books/course material 1,000 + personal 2,700. Travel is not in this total: the aid office says it varies by home address; the CDS 2025-26 G5 lists 1,100 for transportation (with travel, 99,085). Yale does not print a single total on the page.

aidPromise.text: Families with incomes below $100,000 and typical assets qualify for a zero parent share award covering tuition and fees, housing, food and travel, plus hospitalization insurance coverage and a $2,000 start-up grant in the first year. Families with incomes below $200,000 and typical assets receive a need-based scholarship covering at least tuition. Need-blind admission for any student anywhere in the world; aid meets 100% of demonstrated need regardless of citizenship or immigration status, without requiring loans.
aidPromise.year: current policy as published for 2026-27 (start year of the $200,000 tier not stated on the page)

facts.text: Yale's early plan is Single-Choice (Restrictive) Early Action, non-binding, due November 1; Yale states it gives no advantage to applicants who apply early, and students denied early cannot reapply in Regular Decision the same year.

Families earning under $100,000 with typical assets pay nothing (zero parent share, travel included, plus a $2,000 start-up grant); under $200,000, aid covers at least full tuition; 21% of students' families pay nothing.

Admission is need-blind for every applicant worldwide, and aid meets 100% of demonstrated need regardless of citizenship, with no loans in initial offers; 88% of Yale College graduates have no student loan debt.
Testing tightened: the class entering fall 2025 applied under a test-flexible policy (ACT, SAT, AP or IB), while current applicants must submit the SAT or ACT.
For fall 2025, 944 applicants were offered a place on the waiting list, 738 accepted it and 32 were admitted.
Yale's 2026-27 tuition is $72,500, with housing $12,080 and food $9,520.

notes: Cycle from CDS 2025-26 (file dated 2026-06-16). CDS C8F still describes the test-flexible policy (ACT, AP, IB; the CDS text lists 'ACT' twice, apparently a typo for SAT) that applied to the fall 2025 class; the admissions page today requires ACT or SAT. The page does not give the date of the change; web search quota was exhausted before I could find the official announcement, so testPolicy.since is null. GPA (C11-C12) left blank by Yale. CDS G1 lists 2026-27 tuition 72,500 and food and housing 21,600 but leaves required fees blank, while the aid office COA lists a 185 student activity fee. No official class of 2030 (fall 2026) counts found. The start year of the $200,000 no-tuition tier could not be confirmed (news.yale.edu URL guessed returned 404).
